newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle seen steady to up, feeders lower.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle seen steady to up, feeders lower.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open steady to 0.150 cent higher while feeder cattle futures were called 0.200 to 0.500 cent lower, livestock analysts said.

Weather concerns prompted by wintry weather and sub zero wind chills were expected to support live cattle futures. Fed cattle weights were running well under last year's level and the cold snap will add to the decline, analysts said.
They also cited continued good boxed beef movement at lower prices which likely indicates that the beef market is near a bottom.

Feeder cattle futures were seen under pressure following release of USDA date on U.S. grain stocks and production. The report is called bullish to corn prices and this will pressure feeders. Traders had expected the report to show larger corn stocks, analysts said.
However, losses may be limited by another gain in the latest CME feeder cattle index and expected continued good demand for replacement feeders at feedlots, they added.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was up $0.49 at $67.58 per cwt.
